text:
Luke Evangelista came to New Jersey from Nashville and walked into a team that has won nine of its last ten. He's playing 17 minutes a night, and the Devils take 64.3% of the 5v5 expected goals (the quality of the chances) with him on the ice, 7.7 points better than without him.

The points haven't followed the play. He has 10 in 15 games, and the Devils have scored 5.6 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there, which has cost him points. That usually swings back. His goal against the Islanders on Nov. 7, which Mike Fink of The Hockey News described as going in off Ilya Sorokin's back, is the kind of break he has been owed.

Evolving-Hockey rated his 2025-26 at 3.5 wins above replacement, 6th among forwards, while warning that his results ran ahead of his chances. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 89th percentile in primary shot assists. He's a passer, and the Devils are giving him passers' minutes.
headline: Evangelista fits in New Jersey, the goals lag
